Three directions, one stance.

Codex and Grok were asked independently for a direction. They converged: this should read like a tax instrument, not a SaaS landing page. Both named the same trap — Codex: "this audience interprets missing detail as missing capability"; Grok: "they read a Linear-style page as a startup, not someone who will pick up at 9pm."

So none of these three is minimal-and-airy. They differ in what the hero LEADS with.

Pick one and I'll build it out across the site.

The axis being tested:

A leads with the compliance promise, proof in a dashboard.
B leads with the artefact — the invoice FBR stamped.
C leads with the firm's arithmetic — 18 clients, 3 filings due.

A is safest. B is the most distinctive and hardest to copy. C converts accountants fastest but risks losing the single-business buyer.

September and October were doing too much work as one example, so the worked example is now a five-month ledger with the wallet balance carried down the right-hand side.

The two things a client needs to believe are both visible: October costs nothing, and a busy September does not push October onto a higher rate.

Rows animate in one after another so the balance reads as a sequence rather than a table.

THREE NUMBERS DISAGREE between the Aug-26 brochure, the live site, and what you told me. I have not silently picked a winner.

1. Signup credit. You: pay 5,000, get 10,500, less 4,500 integration, 6,000 left. Brochure: pay 5,000, get 7,500 credit AND integration free — which leaves 7,500. The brochure offer is better and says "15 maheena".

2. Fair use. You said 30,000/month. The brochure says 50,000.

3. Bulk upload. Brochure says 50,000 invoices per file. The live site says 9,000.

The artboards use YOUR numbers where you gave them.

PRA now sits beside FBR as an equal column rather than a separate page nobody finds.

The split that matters to a buyer: FBR is federal and covers goods; PRA is provincial and covers services in Punjab. Plenty of businesses owe both, and today they keep two sets of records to do it.

Neither column carries a price. There is one integration fee of PKR 4,500 and it covers every integration you switch on — stated once, underneath. This matches pra-integration.html, which already says "No separate setup fee".

Modules come from the Aug-26 brochure — General Ledger, P&L, complete books, purchasing, document archive and audit trail are INCLUDED. Payroll (Rs 100/employee) and POS+PRA (Rs 1,000/mo) are the paid add-ons.

STILL OPEN, and it is about MONTHLY pricing rather than setup: the brochure sells PRA inside the POS add-on at Rs 1,000/month, while pra-integration.html bills PRA on its own 500/1,000/2,000/3,000 brackets on top of FBR. A business filing both would pay very different amounts under each.
